HEEWON STYLE — a KOREAN WEBTOON movie still PAINTED like a premium digital painting, the look of a dramatic manhwa cover. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). The shot the scene names (wide establishing, two-shot, close-up, over-the-shoulder) from a dramatic camera angle (low three-quarter, worm's-eye, high overhead or dutch), never a flat straight-on catalogue pose. Named characters' FACES are drawn exactly like the attached character sheet: the same confident ink linework drawn BOLD and THICK with real line weight — a heavy tapered black contour around the whole silhouette and the hair mass, medium lines for folds and features, fine lines only for lashes and loose strands and manhwa face design (eye shape, brows, nose, jaw, hairline and hair), recognisably those characters, in the clothes the scene gives them. EVERYTHING ELSE IS PAINTED: visible textured brushwork — loose digital-paint strokes and dry-brush, charcoal-like hatching that follow every fold of the silk and every plate of armour, the shadows built from layered strokes, the brightest ridges laid in with single confident strokes, a faint paper-and-canvas grain; at the edges of the garments the linework breaks into loose sketchy strokes. MYTHIC PAINTED FINISH: rich saturated jewel-tone colour, never a muddy grey-brown wash; splashed sumi-ink spatter and dry-brush flying-white streaks breaking out at the frame edges; ONE bold sweeping painted ribbon of the scene's accent colour (cloth, smoke, banner, mist or light) carving across the composition like a brushstroke of legend. NOT flat cel-shading, NOT smooth airbrushed gradients, NOT a clean vector look, NOT photoreal, NOT 3D. BOLD KOREAN WEBTOON movie still — thick black ink contours, hard cel-shade, glossy graphic highlights. NOT photoreal, NOT oil painting, NOT 3D, NOT Caravaggio. Night interior, Sabi banquet hall. HARD DUTCH, worm's-eye from the floor beside a spilled bronze cup. ONE device: the dais as a dark wedge; the open door a thin gold rectangle behind the councillor. King Euija LARGE in the upper-right third, heavy, bearded, crimson silk, yellow-gold headband, drunk and loud, one knee up on the dais, pointing a wine cup at the door, mouth open mid-accusation, not a standing portrait. Tiny in the door at the far left: Councillor Sunchung, vermilion robe, white hair, black cap with the front gold flame, sleeves hanging, mouth unfinished. Empty benches recede. A low oil lamp set on the floor beside the lens rakes UP across the king's silk and the wet cup; orange #e08a2e as real lamp bounce, not a glow; gold #c9a24d a thin catch on Sunchung in the door. Walls at an angle, his cast shadow climbing the plaster. No crowd — the king, the door, the cup. EXACTLY two named people. Composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop. REFERENCE SHEET. TOP ROW, left to right: LEFT face = euija, SECOND face = seongchung. Copy each face exactly; give each person the dress the scene names. SMALLER SECOND ROW, left to right: place board pl_sabi_palace (keep this exact architecture and ground), costume chart (cut and shape only; ignore its labels, poses and faces), crown reference (shape only). KING EUIJA — Look: Broad, bearded king; black hair in a topknot with a yellow-gold headband whose tails trail; heavy brows, cynical eyes. Dress: Crimson robe with a dark charcoal collar and gold trim; a steel lamellar pauldron peeking at one shoulder. Crown: Baekje king: a tall rounded black silk cap (오라관) with a plain black band at the brow, and a pair of tall openwork gold flame-and-leaf ornaments (금제관식) pinned to either side of the cap, rising above it like twin flames — thin gold blades fanning upward with leaf buds and curls. On Euija the two side ornaments are King Muryeong's gold diadem ornaments exactly as the attached museum photo (ignore its backdrop): a pair of thin sheet-gold flame-and-honeysuckle sprays, each a central stem with curling leaf-flames fanning up and out, pierced openwork and hung with small round gold spangles, one pinned on each side of the black silk cap and rising well above it. Colour #e08a2e. SUNCHUNG — Look: Elderly Baekje councillor: long white hair falling past the shoulders from under a small black silk cap with a single gold openwork flame-and-phoenix ornament pinned at the FRONT of the cap; full white beard and white moustache; heavy-lidded tired eyes, a deep crease between the brows, sun-weathered skin. Dress: Deep vermilion-red wide-sleeved court robe over a cream crossed inner collar, a dark indigo-blue sash, two carved jade toggles and a long red tassel hanging at the waist. Colour #c9a24d. PLACE Sabi (사비 (부여)) — attached board /pl_sabi_palace.png; keep this exact architecture and ground. Sabi palace on the Baengma river bluffs; Baekje giwa halls and pavilions. BACKGROUND AND LIGHT (painterly tenebrism): the background IS the place and the moment of the scene — open sky if they are in the sky, the hall if they are in a hall, the gate, the river, the snow — painted loosely in atmospheric brushwork (drifting smoke, cloud, haze, mist, falling snow, embers) in the scene's own colours, soft and out of focus, with a faint bokeh of small lights; it has colour, weather and depth — never a flat black void, never a detailed set; crowds and armies only as massed painted shapes dissolving into haze. ONE hard directional key light that belongs to the place (a brazier, a lamp, the sun through cloud, a torch, moonlight) rakes across the faces and clothes from the side or from below, modelling them in high contrast with deep painted shadows and a thin edge of the same light along the silhouette. Each character's colour lives in that light and in the atmosphere around them — never a glow aura or halo. Faces and bodies act the beat: real expressions, real weight, mid-motion. Faces from the sheet; new poses, never the sheet's stance. Each named person appears once, never cloned. Everyone wears period clothing of their own court (Korean, Tang, Yamato, Mohe furs), never European dress. No text, no speech bubbles, no panel borders, no watermark. NIGHT GROUND: the frame is built on BLACK — crushed ink-black night masses around the subject, the place pulled out of the dark only where the one key light (fire, lamp, torch, moon) falls, small warm bokeh in the black; the figure is the bright thing in a dark frame.
